criteria.evidence: Registration by link and with a password both create an account; with a password the first login is closed until the address is confirmed. End-to-end on the real stack with Mailpit (web/tests/e2e/115-password-login.spec.ts, steps 1-4): the account is created with emailVerifiedAt = null and a $argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$ hash that does not contain the password; loginWithPassword before confirmation returns email_unconfirmed, no session row appears; the /auth/confirm?token= link from the letter confirms the address and issues a session; the same link a second time renders the invalid state. Resolver-level duplicates in server/tests/auth-password.test.ts ('creates the account without address confirmation', 'does not let in by password before confirmation', 'confirms the address, issues a session and burns the link').

An account created by a magic link stays passwordless and signs in by link: e2e scenario 'an account created by a link stays passwordless and signs in by link' checks passwordHash = null and emailVerifiedAt set after the link exchange, then sets the first password on /me/password and signs in with it. server/tests/auth-magic-link.test.ts additionally covers that a link login into an unconfirmed password registration confirms the address and drops that password, while a confirmed account keeps its password.

Password reset goes by e-mail and no answer discloses whether the account exists. server/tests/auth-password.test.ts: requestPasswordReset returns an identical payload for an existing and an unknown address and sends the letter only to the existing one; loginWithPassword returns the same UNAUTHENTICATED extensions and message for an unknown address and for a wrong password (the unknown address is verified against a dummy hash of equal cost); registerWithPassword answers a taken address exactly as a free one and leaves the other account's password untouched, the owner of the mailbox gets a 'you already have an account' letter. e2e: reset link from the letter sets a new password, the old one stops working and the new one signs in.

Login attempts are limited by the owner-approved thresholds RL-14 and RL-15 (journal §44 item 1): server/tests/auth-password.test.ts section 'лимит попыток входа по паролю' - five failed attempts on one address answer UNAUTHENTICATED and the sixth answers RATE_LIMITED with a positive retryAfter while a neighbouring address is unaffected; a successful check clears the address bucket, so there is no permanent lockout; the request-address bucket rejects the thirty-first attempt spread over different accounts; rate_limit.hit carries the bucket and contains neither the address nor the password. Only failed password checks are counted: the buckets are applied in the resolver, not in the middleware.
